A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SplatPainter, with matching authors, architecture and retained experiments. The main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original local-refinement and relighting experiments, compression and TTT ablations, and editing results on generated assets in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative creative-editing comparisons, conflicting-input results and additional appendix comparisons.

M1.justification: The voxel-compression and TTT pipeline, reconstruction losses, local voxel selection and Gaussian decoding remain unchanged (Section 3; Appendices A.1-A.2). v2's clarification that decoding updates geometry and appearance repeats information already present in v1's method and appendix.

E1.justification: Objaverse/TexVerse data and Trellis-generated assets remain the represented domains; local refinement, painting and relighting already appear in v1. v2 adds mutually inconsistent editing views as a distinct input scenario (Figure 13). The ten-asset creative-editing comparison otherwise extends existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds VoxHammer and VineDresser3D to quantitative and qualitative creative-editing comparisons, and evaluates DGE qualitatively rather than merely citing it. Direct 3DGS optimization joins the global-relighting comparison. The local-refinement comparator set is retained; cross-attention was already evaluated in v1's TTT ablation.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a quantitative editing protocol on ten Trellis assets with shared Nano Banana 2 guidance and separate PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS measurements for edit fidelity and preservation of unedited regions (Table 3; Appendix A.3). Its added relighting optimization baseline fixes geometry while optimizing SH and opacity. Core training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a conflicting-input case study testing which edit persists (Figure 13), plus visual and error-map evidence supplementing the existing TTT-versus-cross-attention ablation (Figure 11). Compression and input-view-count analyses are largely retained; rearranging the iterative-relighting display does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The ten assets in the added creative-editing evaluation constitute a sample size, not repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports edited/unedited-region PSNR of 25.61/33.02 for SplatPainter, 11.25/13.86 for VoxHammer and 11.99/15.79 for VineDresser3D. Table 2 adds 3DGS relighting results and cross-attention metrics beyond its previously reported 24.05 PSNR. Existing local-refinement, ReLitLRM, SplatPainter relighting and compression-table values remain unchanged. New qualitative comparisons and conflicting-input findings, plus a replaced compression example, expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The voxel aggregation, TTT adaptation and reconstruction-loss mathematics in Equations (1)-(9) are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The three enumerated contributions remain state-aware feedforward editing through TTT, versatile local/global applications, and quality at interactive speed. v2 foregrounds appearance lifting and identity preservation, but these capabilities and the central contribution claims were already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing structured-latent editing leakage to global receptive fields and interpreting local updates as preserving untouched content bit-exactly. It also explains conflicting edits as favoring the latest input. The existing limitation concerning new geometry remains, with a modest expansion of future-work discussion.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 documents baseline input preparation, shared Nano Banana 2 guidance and the relighting optimizer's adjustable attributes. Existing architecture and training details are retained. However, v2 omits v1's explicit TexVerse 4K/8K subset designation, bicubic preprocessing specification and evaluation-view counts; these omissions do not establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to VoxHammer, VineDresser3D, Nano Banana 2 and native compact structured latents. Related work introduces direct structured-latent editing as a third paradigm and positions SplatPainter against spatial leakage. Most prior literature remains; the additional Trellis publication entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. v2 centralizes baseline discussion, divides local editing into refinement and creative-editing subsections, reorganizes baseline details into Appendix A.3, and places supplementary material before references. Much of the method and training prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 changes from two-column to single-column formatting, consolidates four tables, redraws the TTT schematic, and rearranges existing result panels. It adds creative-editing, cross-attention, conflicting-input and appendix comparison figures. The iterative-relighting figure is transposed and reduced, while one compression example is replaced.

improvement.justification: The creative-editing comparisons and conflict test strengthen evidence for capabilities previously illustrated mainly through examples, and Appendix A.3 improves baseline transparency. These gains are limited by the ten-example evaluation, lost protocol details and the new bit-exact preservation claim, which Table 3's nonzero unedited-region errors do not establish. Overall, v2 provides useful additional validation without changing the method or existing aggregate findings.
